newsitem.title: UK: UPS unions outline May 22 action plans.
newsitem.headline: UPS unions outline May 22 action plans.

text.p: United Parcel Service of America workers in Europe and North America will hold rallies on May 22 in a day of action to support improved working conditions, the International Federation of Transport Workers (ITF) said.
The rallies have been called by the World UPS Trade Union Council formed this February at a meeting in London, the ITF statement added.

The London-based organisation said rallies are expected at UPS' headquarters in Atlanta, at its European headquarters in Brussels as well as at work locations in Italy, Spain, France, the Netherlands, Germany, Ireland, the U.S., Canada and Brazil.
No comment on the proposed action was immediately available from UPS' Brussels headquarters.
The U.S. Teamsters union, whose four-year UPS contract is up for renewal this July, is a member of the World UPS Trade Union Council and is supporting the day of action.
Teamster President Ron Carey said: "The problems our members face in the U.S. are repeated everywhere UPS does business," according to the statement.

It added that issues of particular concern to UPS workers were the company's shift to using more subcontractors and owner-drivers, the trend towards part-time jobs instead of full-time work and the need for a safer work place.

The statement said that in June there will be a Washington D.C. meeting of union leaders represented on the World Council. The agenda will include the need for a code of conduct for UPS in addressing its workers' problems. --Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542-7706 Fax+5017
